decision: Retain the offline service candidate. All three full arms authenticate; strict/earlier-consent save 11/52 mock calls with about one second median added read latency. Collector adaptation and study continuity require closed-loop qualification before any live proposal.
falsifier: Wrong original obligation, changed accepted input, fabricated receipt availability, lost or late delivery, bad cost attribution, or failed frozen-collector continuity would weaken or invalidate adoption.
hypothesis: Full physical collector-path replay can quantify whether duplicate-call savings survive process startup, queue, delivery and correlated-failure costs under explicit timing consent.
limitations: Single sequential fixed historical replay with fabricated HTTP and real process/IPC overhead; no repeated-run uncertainty estimate.
Independent arm uses a common single-attempt primitive, not all five actual frozen collector loops.
Harness iteration completion is not collector ingestion; adapter API return/acknowledgement/receipt semantics remain unqualified.
Earlier-time sharing requires explicit proposed consent; adaptive retries, recovery, cancellation, rate feedback and unknown external-IP headroom remain unqualified.
Current peer guard counts independent receipts correctly; hypothetical shared receipts require authenticated transport identity before deduplication.
Financial benefit is not established and sealed prospective economics were not evaluated.
Service deployment, original-study continuity, long-duration resource retention and dynamic connections remain unqualified.
